title_ar: بادر قبل فوات الأوان !! | فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو
title_en: Act Before It Is Too Late!! | The Eminent Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew
body_ar: احرص على أداء الحقوق التي عليك قبل فوات الأوان و هذه التبعات التي تقعد بالإنسان عن الطاعات و تقعد به عن المنازل العالية بادر بردها قبل أن تحين ساعة الأجل. 1- حق الوالدين حقهما عظيم جدا، تعاهدهما في كل يوم ، حاول أن تحسن إليهما امتثالا لأمر الله في كل يوم تطلع فيه الشمس بإحسان جديد نوع أنواع الإحسان إليهما حتى تنال برهما و حتى تتقرب منهما، لا تكن من الذين يقتصرون على ما تعودوا عليه من البرور في الصبا فيكون برورهم قاصرا عند ذلك الحد، حاول أن تكون صاحب إبداع ، كل يوم لديك إحسان جديد لم يعهداه منك من قبل. كلما تقدم بهما العمر وجدا فيك من البر و لين الجانب ما ينوهان به كما قال الرجل في وصف ولده رأيت رباطاً حين تم شبابه .. وولي شبابي ليس في بره عتب لنا جانب منه يلين وجانب ... ثقيلٌ على الأعداء مركبه صعب يخبرني عما سألت بهين ... من القول لا جافي الكلام ولا لغب ولا يبتغي أمناً وصاحب رحله ... بخوفٍ إذا ما ضم صاحبه الجنب وتَأخذهُ عِندَ الْمكارمِ هــــــــــــــزَةٌ ... كَما اهتزَ تَحتَ الْبارِحِ الْفننُ الرَّطبُ حاول أن تكون محسنا إلى والديك سواء كانا في الأحياء أو في الأموات، ففي الأموات إبداعك كل يوم في التفنن في صلة أرحامهما ووصل قراباتهما و القيام بكل عمر صالح كانا يقومان به و إنفاذ وصيتهما و الدعاء لهما و الصدقة عنهما كل ذلك يكون إبداعا في برهما بعد الممات؛ 2- كذلك أداء حق الزوجة و الزوج فقد أوصى الله تعالى بهما فقال " { .. وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنبِ .. } الصاحب بالجنب الزوج و الزوجة فلا بد من الإبداع في أداء التبعات و أداء الحق ، فكل واحد منهما له حق على الآخر كما قال الله تعالى : { وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ } فلا بد من أداء تلك الحقوق و التبعات و السعي للإبداع في الإحسان الذي أمر الله به . 3- كذلك الجيران ما زال جبريل يحثني على الجار حتى ظننت أنه سيورثه ، و كثير منا الآن لا يعرف جيرانه الأقربين و لا يهتم باهتماماتهم و لا يؤمل آمالهم ولا يتألم بآلامهم و الجار حقه عظيم فإن كان مؤمنا فله حقان و إن كان كافرا فله حق 4- ثم بعد ذلك أداء حقوق الأقربين الذين أمر الله بالإحسان إليهم حتى بالوصية لهم { كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا الْوَصِيَّةُ لِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ ۖ حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ } ما يتعلق بالوالدين نسخ لكن بقي ما يتعلق بالأقربين؛ و النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أتاه أبو طلحة الأنصاري رضي الله عنه فذكر أنه سمع قول الله تعالى : { لَن تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ ۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُوا مِن شَيْءٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ } و أنه لا يملك مالا هو خير من بيرحاء فأمره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يجعلها في قرابته فوزعها بينهم؛ هذه صلة الرحم التي هي حق عظيم لما قضى الله خلق الخلق قامت الرحم فتعلقت بساق العرش، فقالت: يا رب! هذا مقام العائذ بك من القطيعة، فقال:( أما ترضين أن أصل من وصلك وأقطع من قطعك ) قالت رضيت و قد قال الله تعالى : { فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الأرْضِ وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ (٢٢) أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ فَأَصَمَّهُمْ وَأَعْمَى أَبْصَارَهُمْ } و قد قال البخاري رحمه الله تعالى : ( صلة الرحم إشراك القرابات فيما أوتي الإنسان من أنواع الخيرات ) إذا أوتي علما يعلمهم ، إذا أوتي دعوة صالحة يدعو لهم، إذا أوتي مالا يعطيهم، إذا أوتي جاها يشفع لهم و هكذا. فيسعى الإنسان لصلتهم لأن الحقوق الدنيوية تقعد بالإنسان عن المقامات العالية ، قد يثقل ظهر الإنسان بكثرة ما تحمله من الديون و الحقوق فلا يوفق للطاعات و المقامات الكبيرة، لكن إذا تخلص من تلك التبعات استطاع الاسراع على الطريق و كان من السابقين الذينقال الله فيهم ( وَمِنْهُمْ سَابِقٌ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْكَبِيرُ .. }
body_en:
Be diligent in discharging the rights owed by you before it is too late. These liabilities are what hold a person back from acts of obedience and keep him from the high stations; hasten to render them back before the hour of death comes.

**1 — The right of the parents.** Their right is very great indeed. Attend to them every day. Try to do good to them, in compliance with God's command, with some fresh kindness on every day the sun rises. Vary the kinds of good you do them, so that you may attain dutifulness towards them and draw near to them. Do not be one of those who confine themselves to the dutifulness they grew used to in childhood, so that their dutifulness stops short at that limit. Try to be a person of invention: every day you have some new kindness that they have not known from you before. As they advance in years, let them find in you such dutifulness and such gentleness that they speak of it with praise — as the man said, describing his son:

*I saw a tethered steed when his youth had come to its fullness and my own youth had turned away; in his dutifulness there is nothing to reproach.*

*Towards us there is a side of him that softens, and a side heavy upon his enemies, hard to ride.*

*He tells me what I have asked of him in speech made easy, neither rough in its words nor idle.*

*He does not seek safety for himself while the companion of his journey is in fear, when his companion's side is pressed close to his own.*

*A thrill takes hold of him at the call of noble deeds, as the green bough quivers beneath the hot wind.*

Try to be one who does good to your parents, whether they are among the living or among the dead. In the case of the dead, your inventiveness lies in finding some new way each day of keeping ties with their kin and joining their relations; in performing every righteous deed they used to perform; in executing their will; in praying for them and giving charity (ṣadaqah) on their behalf. All of that is inventiveness in dutifulness to them after death.

**2 — Likewise, rendering the right of the wife and of the husband.** God the Exalted enjoined care for them both, saying: {… and the companion at your side …} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:36). "The companion at your side" is the husband and the wife. So there must be inventiveness in discharging one's liabilities and rendering what is due, for each of the two has a right over the other, as God the Exalted said: {And they have rights similar to those due from them, according to what is right; and men have a degree over them} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:228). So those rights and liabilities must be discharged, and one must strive for inventiveness in the good conduct God has commanded.

**3 — Likewise the neighbours.** "Gabriel kept on urging me concerning the neighbour, until I thought he would make him an heir." Many of us today do not know our nearest neighbours, take no interest in what concerns them, do not hope their hopes, and feel no pain at their pains. The neighbour's right is great: if he is a believer he has two rights, and if he is an unbeliever he has one.

**4 — Then after that, rendering the rights of near relatives,** whom God has commanded us to treat well, even to the point of making a bequest to them: {It is prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you and he leaves behind wealth, that he make a bequest to parents and near relatives according to what is right — a duty upon the God-conscious} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:180). What relates to the parents has been abrogated (mansūkh), but what relates to near relatives remains.

And when Abu Talha al-Ansari (may God be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and mentioned that he had heard the word of God the Exalted, {You will not attain righteousness until you spend of what you love; and whatever you spend, God knows it} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:92), and that he owned no property dearer to him than Bayruha, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) ordered him to place it among his relatives, and he distributed it among them.

This is the keeping of kinship ties, which is a great right. When God had decreed the creation of creation, the womb rose and clung to the leg of the Throne, and said: "My Lord! This is the station of one who seeks refuge with You from severance." He said: "Are you not content that I should join whoever joins you, and cut off whoever cuts you off?" It said: "I am content." And God the Exalted has said: {Would you then, if you turned away, spread corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? (22) Those are the ones whom God has cursed, so He made them deaf and blinded their eyes} (Sūrat Muhammad 47:22–23).

And al-Bukhari (may God the Exalted have mercy on him) said: "Keeping ties of kinship is to give one's relatives a share in whatever kinds of good a person has been given." If he has been given knowledge, he teaches them; if he has been given an answered prayer, he prays for them; if he has been given wealth, he gives to them; if he has been given standing, he intercedes for them; and so on.

So let a person strive to keep ties with them, because worldly obligations hold a person back from the high stations. A person's back may be weighed down by the sheer quantity of debts and dues he has taken upon himself, so that he is not granted success in acts of obedience and in the great stations; but once he is rid of those liabilities he is able to move swiftly along the road, and to be among those who go ahead, of whom God said: {And among them is one who goes ahead in good deeds by God's leave; that is the great bounty} (Sūrat Fāṭir 35:32).

[Translator's note: renderings of Qur'anic verses here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.]

flags.context: Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:228, quoted by the Sheikh to establish that husband and wife each have rights over the other
options: and men have a degree over them
and men have a degree above them
and husbands have a rank over them
flags.note: EDITORIAL. The verse is quoted as scripture, without commentary, and in a passage whose whole point is the MUTUALITY of spousal rights (the immediately preceding clause is "they have rights similar to those due from them"). Translated literally and flagged only because الدرجة is among the most contested phrases in English-language discussion of the Qur’an, and a decontextualised quotation of it carries reputational exposure. No softening has been applied, and the Sheikh offers no gloss of his own that could be reported instead. A display decision, not a translation problem.

flags.arabic: فإن كان مؤمنا فله حقان و إن كان كافرا فله حق
flags.context: the section on the rights of neighbours
options: if he is a believer he has two rights, and if he is an unbeliever he has one
if he is a Muslim he has a double claim, and if he is a non-Muslim a single claim
the believing neighbour has the right of neighbourhood and the right of faith; the unbelieving neighbour has the right of neighbourhood alone
flags.note: EDITORIAL, minor. A standard formulation, and the thrust of the passage is that a non-Muslim neighbour DOES have a right that must be discharged. Rendered literally. Flagged because an English reader meeting "if he is an unbeliever he has one" without the surrounding argument may read a slight where the passage intends an obligation. Option 2 is the explanatory expansion; it has not been used, because the Sheikh does not supply it.

flags.arabic: القيام بكل عمر صالح كانا يقومان به
flags.context: listing the ways of honouring deceased parents
options: a misprint for عمل صالح, "every righteous deed they used to perform"
as written, عمر صالح, "every righteous span of life"
a different word lost in transmission
flags.note: عمر صالح makes no sense with يقومان به ("which the two of them used to perform"), and عمل صالح is a single-letter difference and the obvious reading. Option 0 is used in body_en. The Arabic is preserved uncorrected in body_ar (style guide section 11).

flags.arabic: رأيت رباطاً حين تم شبابه .. وولي شبابي ليس في بره عتب
flags.context: the opening line of the five lines of verse quoted in section 1, introduced as "the man said, describing his son"
options: "I saw a tethered steed" — رباط as a horse kept tied and ready, a classical figure for a son who is his father’s strength
"I saw a firm bond" — رباط as the tie of kinship between them
the text is corrupt and the intended word is not recoverable
flags.note: رِباط bears both senses and the line is elliptical. The poet is not named in the source, and the lines are not attributed to any collection, so they cannot be checked against a text. The fourth line in particular (ولا يبتغي أمناً وصاحب رحله بخوفٍ إذا ما ضم صاحبه الجنب) is obscure and its rendering here is provisional. Translated as prose per style guide section 4; no rhymed English attempted.

flags.arabic: كَما اهتزَ تَحتَ الْبارِحِ الْفننُ الرَّطبُ
flags.context: the closing line of the quoted verse
options: the hot wind (al-bāriḥ, the scorching summer wind of the desert)
a wind blowing from the direction that brings ill omen, on the older augural sense of بارح
flags.note: البارح names a specific hot wind in classical usage, but the word also carries an augural sense. The image — a green bough quivering — works with any of them. Not resolved.

translator_notes: A written lecture, filed by the site under the mohadarrat (lectures) category. Typed "transcript". The text is continuous and reaches a proper conclusion that returns to its opening theme, so it has NOT been marked source_is_excerpt_only; there is no .docx download link on the page.

category_ar and category_en are derived from the URL alias "mohadarrat" (محاضرات, lectures); the page itself does not print a breadcrumb, so the Arabic category label has not been read directly from the source and should be confirmed.

إبداع is the organising word of the whole lecture and is rendered consistently as "invention / inventiveness" rather than being varied for style, since the Sheikh is making a point about constantly finding NEW ways to discharge a duty.

The gloss "The companion at your side is the husband and the wife" is the Sheikh’s own reading of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:36 and is kept as his. The classical exegetes also read الصاحب بالجنب as the travelling companion; that alternative is not in the source and has not been introduced.

The ruling in section 4 that "what relates to the parents has been abrogated (mansūkh), but what relates to near relatives remains" is the Sheikh’s own statement about Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:180 and is rendered exactly, with no supporting argument added and none removed.

THREE HADITHS ARE QUOTED WITHOUT ATTRIBUTION OR GRADING: the report of Gabriel and the neighbour; the report of Abu Talha and Bayruha; and the report of the womb clinging to the Throne. The Sheikh gives no narrator, collection or grading for any of them, so none has been supplied (style guide section 4). The quotation from al-Bukhari on صلة الرحم IS attributed in the source and the attribution is preserved.
Renderings of Qur’anic verses are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic; a standing note to that effect is carried at the foot of body_en.

Note that NO addslashes backslashes appear anywhere in this record, or anywhere in IDs 1105-1210.

SOURCE DEFECT, encoding. The Qur’anic quotations in this record are not encoded consistently: in Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:180, Sūrat Muhammad 47:22-23 and Sūrat Fāṭir 35:32 the shaddah precedes the vowel sign, while in Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:228 and Sūrat Āl ʻImrān 3:92 it follows it. The verses were evidently pasted from two different digital sources. body_ar reproduces the source byte for byte, including this inconsistency; any downstream normalisation should be applied corpus-wide rather than per record.
